findings.title: Empty updateMany throws after cache is written
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache finishes by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is empty (Argument `data` is missing / at least one field required), and this check happens even on models with @updatedAt, so the call throws every time. The free/busy rows are already upserted before this line, with no transaction, so Google webhook and watch refresh callers see a failure and retry. Each retry hits the Google freebusy API again, rewrites the cache, and throws again, which can burn calendar API quota and mark sync as failed. Passing {} also does not achieve the comment's goal: the settings UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt (already maintained by the upsert's @updatedAt), not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Remove this call, or if a touch is actually required set updatedAt: new Date() explicitly.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh cache status
findings.body: deleteCache.useMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. It never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component which invalidates that query in onSettled. cacheUpdatedAt comes from that query, and SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads it with refetchOnWindowFocus: false. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old timestamp and the delete action, so the UI claims cache exists when the rows are gone. onChanged is optional and is not guaranteed to refetch this query, so the mutation itself needs to invalidate connectedCalendars.

findings.title: Cache status treats expired rows as live
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups every CalendarCache row for the credential and returns max(updatedAt), with no expiresAt >= now() filter. getCachedAvailability in the same repository only serves rows that have not expired, so the settings dropdown can show a last-updated time and a delete action for cache that availability lookups will ignore. The new migration also backfills updatedAt to NOW() for every existing row, including expired ones, so right after deploy those stale rows look freshly updated. Filter to non-expired rows (and treat no matching row as no cache) so the status matches what is actually served.

findings.title: Expected auth failure is thrown as a generic Error
findings.body: When the credential is missing or not owned by ctx.user, deleteCacheHandler throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied"). tRPC maps a plain Error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so a normal not-found/forbidden case becomes a 500, gets reported as an exception, and is not a TRPCError the client can distinguish. Use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN instead.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted en-US
findings.body: The last-updated label is built with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }) even though useLocale() is already in this component and the string is translated. Non-English users see an English date format (and the key is not formatted with their locale), which is wrong for a new user-facing timestamp in an i18n app.

findings.title: Webhook helper writes the wrong env file and is macOS-only
findings.body: ENV_FILE is the CWD-relative path ../.env, and the script never cds to its own directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual invocation) updates a .env outside the repo, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never set for the app. The update also uses sed -i '' (line 68), which is BSD/macOS sed; GNU sed on Linux treats '' as a backup suffix and does not apply the substitution. cleanup() always exits 0, so a failed URL extract looks successful to a caller.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared npx tsx
findings.body: dev:cron was changed from ts-node (declared in this package's devDependencies) to npx tsx, but tsx is not a dependency of apps/web. Under Yarn Berry, npx does not reliably resolve workspace binaries and may download an unpinned tsx or fail offline, so yarn dev:cron can break. This change is unrelated to calendar cache and should use a declared runner instead of npx.
